name: FOCUS

foundation.via: A Joint Development Foundation series that the FinOps Foundation funds and staffs; its Governing Board appoints the steering committee

license: Specification under CC BY 4.0; contributions under the project’s contributor licence agreement
summary: The FinOps Open Cost and Usage Specification: one schema for billing data, so cost exports from clouds, SaaS vendors and data centres land in the same columns with the same meaning.
intro: Every cloud publishes a detailed bill as a table, but each uses its own column names, its own way of showing discounts and its own idea of what a row is. FOCUS defines one format for that data. Its core is the Cost and Usage dataset: one row per charge, with mandatory columns such as BilledCost, EffectiveCost, ListCost and ContractedCost, ChargeCategory (Usage, Purchase, Tax, Credit or Adjustment), ServiceCategory from a fixed list of 19 values such as Compute, Databases and AI and Machine Learning, ServiceProviderName, ResourceId, RegionId and a Tags column holding a JSON object. Each column comes with normative rules: for example, a commitment purchase meant to cover later usage must have an EffectiveCost of 0, so adding up effective cost never counts a prepayment twice. Providers can add their own columns, but only with an `x_` prefix.

FOCUS is a specification, not software. Providers, which it calls data generators, export it themselves: in October 2026 the project listed AWS, Microsoft, Google Cloud, Oracle, Alibaba Cloud, Huawei Cloud, IBM Cloud, Cloudflare, Snowflake, Databricks, MongoDB and Vercel among them, each at its own version. Version 1.4, ratified on June 4, 2026, added Billing Period and Invoice Detail datasets, next to Cost and Usage and Contract Commitment, and 47 new columns, so a team can reconcile usage with invoices and track commitments. The text is under CC BY 4.0. The project is a series of the Joint Development Foundation, the Linux Foundation’s home for standards, supported by the FinOps Foundation, and is run by a steering committee and maintainers from cloud providers, tool vendors and large users.
strengths: One query works across providers: AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Oracle and many SaaS and data platforms export it natively
Precise rules for discounts and commitments, with separate billed, effective, list and contracted costs on every row
Built by the providers and their biggest customers together, with a public GitHub process and a conformance programme for data generators
Grows beyond cloud: SaaS, data platforms and data centres, with token-based AI pricing planned for 1.5
limits: Providers lag the spec: in October 2026 most exported 1.0 or 1.2, while 1.4 was current, and AWS’s and Google’s native exports sat at 1.2
Normalised columns hide detail: the provider’s own export, or its `x_` columns, still carry information FOCUS has no column for
Versions are not strict compatibility promises; 1.3 deprecated ProviderName and 1.4 removed it, so queries need updating between versions
Allocation still depends on your tags and account structure: FOCUS standardises the data, not who owns it

sections.intro: FOCUS ships about twice a year, usually announced at the FinOps Foundation’s FinOps X conference in June and in November or December.

story: The work started in the FinOps Foundation’s Open Billing working group, where practitioners tried to agree how billing data should look. In January 2023 the group decided to move it into a new Linux Foundation project, set up as a specification so the cloud providers could commit to it. The foundation announced FOCUS in May 2023 with a steering committee chaired by Udam Dewaraja, then head of cloud financial management at Citigroup, and including Google and Microsoft. The plan was to start with infrastructure-as-a-service and then add SaaS, PaaS and on-premises costs.

Version 0.5 came out at FinOps X in June 2023, and the 1.0 preview in November 2023 with AWS, Microsoft, Google Cloud and Oracle as formal contributors and companies such as Capital One, Walmart, Workday and Goldman Sachs. After 1.0 in June 2024, the providers shipped native exports: Google as a BigQuery view, Microsoft in Cost Management exports and AWS in Data Exports, which reached FOCUS 1.2 in November 2025.

Later versions followed what large users needed to close their books: invoice IDs and currencies in 1.2, contract commitments and split costs in 1.3, and invoice reconciliation in 1.4, ratified on June 4, 2026. The same week, the Linux Foundation announced a Tokenomics Foundation that will jointly fund extending FOCUS to token-based AI pricing, which the project plans for 1.5.

choices.why: Earlier tools converted each provider’s format after the fact and broke when it changed. FOCUS asks providers to export it themselves, which is why it was set up as a standards project with the providers on the steering committee.

choices.choice: Four cost columns on every row
choices.why: Finance needs the invoiced amount, teams need cost after discounts and prepayments, and procurement needs list and contracted prices to measure savings. Keeping all four on one row avoids separate datasets that never reconcile.
ChargeCategory and ServiceCategory may only take listed values, so “all compute spend” or “all taxes” means the same thing for every provider, while ServiceName keeps the provider’s own product name.

choices.choice: Custom columns must start with x_
choices.why: Providers can still publish details FOCUS lacks, and the prefix guarantees a future FOCUS column never collides with a provider’s own.

timeline.text: Open Billing work moves to a new LF project in January; FOCUS announced in May; 0.5 in June; 1.0 preview in November
1.2 in June; AWS Data Exports for FOCUS 1.2 generally available in November; 1.3 in December
1.4 ratified June 4; Tokenomics Foundation announced to fund token pricing in FOCUS
